title: pg_basebackup forwards a tar member trailer using a pointer that buffering already advanced past it
live_proof: inspection at the 17.5 pin. bbstreamer_tar.c:220-222 calls `bbstreamer_buffer_until(streamer, &data, &len, mystreamer->pad_bytes_expected)`, which takes `data` and `len` BY ADDRESS. Its body at bbstreamer.h:174-196 reaches `bbstreamer_buffer_bytes(streamer, data, len, target_bytes - buflen)` at :194, and that helper copies the bytes into the streamer's own buffer while advancing `*data` forward and reducing `*len` by the same amount. So on return `data` points PAST the padding, and when the padding completed the chunk, `len` is 0 and `data` is one past the end of the caller's input. bbstreamer_tar.c:225-228 then passes that advanced `data` with length `pad_bytes_expected` to the next streamer, which reads pad_bytes_expected bytes from beyond the input. Upstream replaces the argument with `mystreamer->base.bbs_buffer.data`, the buffer the padding was actually copied into; the pin passes `data`.
object: the input chunk pg_basebackup received from the server, below which nothing is mapped
lifetime_ender: n/a -- the object is live; the defect is a read past its end
shape: a by-address helper advances the caller's cursor and the caller then reuses the old meaning of it
fidelity: real buffering helpers, transcribed caller, REPRODUCED. bbstreamer_buffer_until and bbstreamer_buffer_bytes are copied verbatim from bbstreamer.h:156-196, including the `*data += nbytes` that is the whole defect; the forwarding call is bbstreamer_tar.c:225-228 transcribed, passing `data` as the pin does rather than bbs_buffer.data as the fix does. StringInfo is a stand-in for src/common/stringinfo.c because the buffer's growth policy takes no part in the defect -- all that matters is that the bytes are copied somewhere else. Not reproduced: the tar parsing that reaches BBSTREAMER_MEMBER_TRAILER and computes pad_bytes_expected, which needs a server streaming a base backup.

spatial.oracle: the overrun of the malloc'd object is reported as a domain fault, or the case completes and this arm did not see it. level0 narrows a returned pointer to the bytes requested, not to a size class, so unlike the purecap guest the bound here is the object itself; the host's fault line carries the pc, and the expect_fault_in line the case prints before the defect is what attributes it.
spatial.verdict_note: cause=5 pc=0xe020fad4 in pgclient_consume_content; by function: pgclient_consume_content is the case's declared fault site

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: SIGPROT(34) -- CHERI-DETECTED. The next streamer reads pad_bytes_expected bytes from a pointer bbstreamer_buffer_until had already advanced to one past the end of the chunk, so the first byte read is already out of bounds. CheriBSD riscv64-purecap, static build, 2026-10-06. The PG_DEFECT marker printed before the fault, so the setup provably ran and the fault is the defective access rather than something earlier. Fault attributed to the defect, 2026-10-06: the case declares the function its fault belongs to and the handler reports the faulting PC and return address as offsets from it. signal=34 si_code=1, pc-expect=+58 against pgclient_consume_content: the faulting instruction is 58 bytes into the next streamer, which is the consumer bbstreamer_tar.c:225 hands the advanced pointer to.
cheribsd-revocation.run: run 2026-10-06 by the corpus's own runner (shared/run-arm.py for the Capstone arms, shared/run-cheribsd.sh for the purecap one); see results/

host-asan.oracle: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow, READ of size 1, "0 bytes to the right of 24-byte region", in pgclient_consume_content (the next streamer) called from case.c:58. The 24-byte region is the input chunk and 24 is pad_bytes_expected. Two notes print first and establish the mechanism rather than asserting it: remaining_len=0 and data_past_end=1, i.e. bbstreamer_buffer_until consumed the whole chunk and left `data` exactly one past its end, which is the pointer bbstreamer_tar.c:225 then forwards. Host build, 2026-10-06.

sublet.oracle: the Sublet application heap (tools/arms.json app-sublet, CAPSTONE_APPLICATION_HEAP=sublet): a domain fault in the function the case names (expect_fault_in, or fault_sites), or the case returns and this arm did not see it. malloc shrinks the alias to the request, so the bounds are the object's rather than the buddy block's, and free revokes -- which is what separates this arm from app-level0 and is checked in the same boot: uaf-malloc must FAULT here and must COMPLETE there. These five call libc malloc directly, so what is measured is the heap's own protection of a non-nested object and not Sublet's sub-allocation unit.

status: measured on all three arms 2026-10-06: spatial=detected, sublet=detected, cheribsd-revocation=detected
nested_why: The object comes straight from libc malloc. Nothing carves it out of a larger block, so it is not nested. libpq does have a nested allocator of its own, pqResultAlloc's PGresult blocks, but none of these five touches that storage.
